Rashi on Keritot 9a:10:1.hebrew: וכי יגור אתכם גר וגו' לדורותיכם - אע"ג דליכא מקדש:
Rashi on Keritot 9a:10:1.english: And if a stranger sojourn with you, etc., throughout your generations - Even though there is no Temple.

Rashi on Keritot 9a:11:1.hebrew: צריך שיפריש רובע דינר לקינו - דלכשיבנה בית המקדש יביא קן, דאמרי' לעיל דצריך קרבן. וקרבן בפחות מרובע לא אפשר להפריש, דאין מצוי קן בפחות מרובע, כדאמרינן במתני': "ועמדו קינין ברבעתים", אבל פחות לא אפשר:
Rashi on Keritot 9a:11:1.english: He must set aside a quarter of a dinar for his bird-nest [offering] - For when the Temple is rebuilt he will bring a bird-nest [offering], as we said above that he requires an offering. And an offering of less than a quarter [of a dinar] cannot be set aside, because a bird-nest [offering] is not available for less than a quarter [of a dinar], as we say in the Mishnah: "and bird-nests stood at two quarters [of a dinar]," but less is not possible.

Rashi on Keritot 9a:11:2.english: Due to the mishap - Lest he derive benefit from it.

Rashi on Keritot 9a:12:1.hebrew: גר תושב - שקבל עליו שלא לעבוד עבודת כוכבים, כגון נעמן:
Rashi on Keritot 9a:12:1.english: A resident alien [ger toshav] - [One] who accepted upon himself not to worship idols, such as Naaman.

Rashi on Keritot 9a:12:2.hebrew: עושה מלאכה בשבת לעצמו - בדבר האבד, כישראל בחולו של מועד:
Rashi on Keritot 9a:12:2.english: Performs labor on Shabbat for himself - In a matter of loss, like a Jew on the intermediate days of a Festival.

Rashi on Keritot 9a:13:1.english: Like a Jew on a Festival - [He is permitted to perform labor for] food preparation.

Rashi on Keritot 9a:14:1.english: The oath of testimony - [He brings] a sliding-scale offering.

Rashi on Keritot 9a:14:2.english: The oath on a deposit - [He brings] a guilt offering.

Rashi on Keritot 9a:17:1.hebrew: מדמצי למיכתב ״על חטאתו״ ולישתוק, וכתיב ״על חטאתו אשר חטא״ — לאתויי חטאים הרבה:
Rashi on Keritot 9a:17:1.english: Since [the verse] could have written “for his sin” and been silent, yet it is written “for his sin that he has sinned,” [this comes] to include many sins.

Rashi on Keritot 9a:17:2.hebrew: ונסלח לו מחטאתו אשר חטא - להכי הדר כתיב תו ב' זימני חטא, בר מב' זימני קמאי, לעשות מזיד כשוגג:
Rashi on Keritot 9a:17:2.english: And he shall be forgiven for his sin that he has sinned - For this reason [Scripture] again wrote "sin" two times, besides the first two times: to render an intentional [transgression] like an unwitting [one].

Rashi on Keritot 9a:19:1.hebrew: ויאמר ה' פתאום - בע"כ יצאו שלשתן ע"פ הדיבור:
Rashi on Keritot 9a:19:1.english: And the Lord spoke suddenly - Against their will, the three of them went out at the [Divine] command.

Rashi on Keritot 9a:20:1.hebrew: ופתאים עברו ונענשו - היינו מזיד, דאין עונש אלא על המזיד:
Rashi on Keritot 9a:20:1.english: But the thoughtless pass on, and are punished - This [refers to] an intentional [transgression], for there is no punishment except for an intentional [transgression].

Rashi on Keritot 9a:22:1.hebrew: ה"א - אע"ג דפתאום דעלמא משמע אונס ושוגג ומזיד, פתאום דנזיר ודאי, מדמייתי קרבן עלה, ש"מ דשוגג הוא, מידי דהוה אכל התורה, דרוב קרבנות על השגגה הן באין. להכי כתיב פתע דהוי שוגג, לגלות עליה דפתאום:
Rashi on Keritot 9a:22:1.english: I would say - Even though pit'om ("suddenly") in general implies duress, unwitting [transgression], and intentional [transgression], [with regard to] the pit'om of a nazirite, certainly since he brings an offering for it, learn from this that it is [referring to] unwitting [transgression], just like the entire Torah, where most offerings are brought for unwitting transgression. Therefore, peta ("suddenly"), which is unwitting [transgression], is written to reveal regarding pit'om.

Rashi on Keritot 9a:24:1.hebrew: בכולן - בכל המביאין עולה ויורד שבאותה פרשה, כגון מטמא מקדש ושבועת בטוי, דכתיבי בהו שבועת העדות:
Rashi on Keritot 9a:24:1.english: With regard to all [of them] - [That is,] with regard to all those who bring a sliding-scale [offering] in that section [of the Torah], such as one who defiles the Temple and [one who takes] an oath of utterance, in which [section] the oath of testimony is written.

Rashi on Keritot 9a:28:1.hebrew: לעשות מזיד כשוגג והא עיקר קרא במזיד כתיב - דכתיב (ויקרא י״ט:כ׳) בקורת תהיה, והיינו מלקות, ואין מלקות אלא במזיד, ועליה קאמר והביא את אשמו. ותו למה לי ונסלח לו מחטאתו לרבות מזיד:
Rashi on Keritot 9a:28:1.english: To render an intentional [transgression] as an unwitting [one]; but the primary verse is written regarding an intentional [transgression] - As it is written (Leviticus 19:20), "There shall be an inspection," and that means lashes, and lashes are [administered] only for an intentional [transgression]; and regarding it, [Scripture] states, "And he shall bring his guilt offering." So why further do I need "and he shall be forgiven for his sin" to include an intentional [transgression]?

Rashi on Keritot 9a:28:2.hebrew: אלא אימא לעשות שוגג כמזיד - דמהו דתימא דוקא אמזיד מביא ולא אשוגג, קא משמע לן "ונסלח לו מחטאתו אשר חטא", דלהכי כתיב "חטא" ארבע זימני: תרי למילף קרבן אחד על עבירות הרבה, ותרי לעשות שוגג כמזיד:
Rashi on Keritot 9a:28:2.english: Rather, say: to make an unwitting [transgression] like an intentional [transgression] - For what might you have said? [That] specifically for an intentional [transgression] he brings [an offering], and not for an unwitting [transgression]; [therefore, Scripture] teaches us: "and he shall be forgiven for his sin that he has sinned," for it is for this reason that "sin" is written four times: two [times] to derive one offering for many transgressions, and two [times] to make an unwitting [transgression] like an intentional [transgression].

Rashi on Keritot 9a:29:1.hebrew: בהעלם אחת - כלומר, קודם שילקה ויביא קרבן על זו, חזר ובעל זו:
Rashi on Keritot 9a:29:1.english: In one lapse of awareness - That is to say, before he would be flogged and bring an offering for this [one], he went back and engaged in intercourse with this [other] one.

Rashi on Keritot 9a:31:1.hebrew: לאו אמרת גבי עריות - בפ"ק (לעיל כריתות ב:), "ואל אשה" — לחלק על כל אשה ואשה כו':
Rashi on Keritot 9a:31:1.english: Did you not state with regard to forbidden relations - In the first chapter (above, Keritot 2b), [the verse] "And unto a woman" [serves] to require separate [offerings] for each and every woman, etc.

Rashi on Keritot 9a:3:1.hebrew: לכם הקשתיו - במקצת, ולא כל קרבנותיכם. ומיהו עולה מסתבר דמכשרא, דכולה כליל:
Rashi on Keritot 9a:3:1.english: I compared him to you - Partially, and not [for] all of your offerings. However, it is reasonable that a burnt offering is valid, because all of it is wholly burned [on the altar].

Rashi on Keritot 9a:4:1.english: Circumcision, immersion, and the sprinkling of blood - [The Gemara] explains [this] below.

Rashi on Keritot 9a:6:1.english: And he shall offer it - Regarding a bird burnt offering [brought as] a freewill offering, in Leviticus.

Rashi on Keritot 9a:6:2.english: And he shall offer - [This] implies a complete offering.

Rashi on Keritot 9a:8:1.english: All the nation that left - At the time of their departure [from Egypt], they were circumcised.

Rashi on Keritot 9a:8:2.english: In your blood - The blood of the Paschal offering and the blood of circumcision.

Rashi on Keritot 9a:9:1.english: Presentation of blood - The sprinkling of blood on the altar.

Tosafot on Keritot 9a:13:1.hebrew: (לעיל. גבי) גר תושב עושה מלאכה לעצמו - מכאן קשה לפ"ה דפרק החולץ (יבמות מח:), דקאמר: "וינפש בן אמתך והגר — זה גר תושב", פי' בקונט' שקיבל עליו שלא לעבוד עבודת כוכבים ומחלל שבת כעובד כוכבים; והכא קאמר גר תושב עושה מלאכה! לכן י"ל דההיא מיירי לענין שלא לעשות מלאכה עבור רבו, אבל לעצמו שרי. (פסק) מכאן פסק ר"י שמותר להניח לעובד כוכבים לעשות מלאכתו בשבת בבית ישראל עבור עצמו:
Tosafot on Keritot 9a:13:1.english: (Above, regarding) "A ger toshav may perform labor for himself" - From here there is a difficulty with the commentary of the Master [Rashi] in the chapter HaCholetz (Yevamot 48b), where [the Gemara] says: "'And the son of your maidservant and the stranger shall be refreshed' — this refers to a ger toshav"; [and] Rashi explained that [a ger toshav is one] who took upon himself not to worship idols, and desecrates Shabbat like an idolater — whereas here it says [that] a ger toshav may perform labor [for himself]! Therefore, one can say that that [passage in Yevamot] is speaking with regard to not performing labor for his master, whereas for himself it is permitted. (Ruling) From here Rabbi Yitzchak ruled that it is permitted to allow an idolater to perform his own work on Shabbat in the house of a Jew for himself.

Tosafot on Keritot 9a:1:1.hebrew: יכול שאני מרבה אפי' מנחה - פירוש: מנחת נסכים, שהיא כולה לאישים:
Tosafot on Keritot 9a:1:1.english: "One might [have thought] that I include even a meal offering" - Explanation: a meal offering [accompanying] libations, which is entirely for the fires [of the altar].

Tosafot on Keritot 9a:3:1.hebrew: ת"ל ככם כגר - מצי למימר כדלעיל: השתא לעוף איתרבאי:
Tosafot on Keritot 9a:3:1.english: "The verse states: 'As you are, so shall the stranger be'" - [The baraita] could have said as above: Now that a bird [offering] was included[, an animal burnt offering is all the more so included].

Tosafot on Keritot 9a:8:1.hebrew: דכתיב כי מולים היו כל העם - פירוש: שמלו עצמם ביציאתם ממצרים. ואע"פ שאותן שהיו נימולים בימי אברהם לא מלו אותם ביציאת מצרים, מ"מ מעיקרא כשמלו עצמן מלו ליכנס בברית המקום וליבדל משאר אומות, וגם כי עתה טבלו:
Tosafot on Keritot 9a:8:1.english: As it is written: "For all the nation was circumcised" - Explanation: that they circumcised themselves upon their exodus from Egypt. And even though those who were circumcised in the days of Abraham were not circumcised [again] at the exodus from Egypt, nevertheless, initially when they circumcised themselves, they circumcised [themselves] to enter into the covenant of the Omnipresent and to separate themselves from the other nations, and also because now they immersed.

Tosafot on Keritot 9a:9:1.hebrew: וישלח את נערי בני ישראל ויעלו עולות - ואע"ג דפליגי התם בפרק פרת חטאת (זבחים קטו), איכא דאמרי עולת ראייה הואי ואיכא דאמרי עולת תמיד [הואי], י"ל שהקריבו הרבה עולות:
Tosafot on Keritot 9a:9:1.english: "And he sent the young men of the children of Israel, and they offered burnt offerings" - Even though they disagree there in the chapter Parat Chatat (Zevachim 115), [where] one says it was a burnt offering of appearance and one says [it was] a daily burnt offering, one can say that they offered many burnt offerings.
